scope: Versioned adjudication of the rigid-direct frame-21 kinematic sweep without changing direct tolerances

adjudication.classification: stale reference from incorrectly realized fixture geometry
adjudication.cause: The command runner reused the dynamic box mesh with 0.25 m half extents for the kinematic body even though the hashed case declares 0.2 m half extents.
adjudication.correction: The shared command runner now creates and selects the declared 0.2 m kinematic mesh. No solver, backend adapter, tolerance or case input changed.
adjudication.historical_observation: The retained pre-correction CPU and CUDA captures place frame-21 contact points at z approximately +/-0.25 m and outside the declared 0.2 m collider.
adjudication.independent_result: Both corrected trajectories pass the geometry, contact-direction, Coulomb-cone, response-sign and planar-symmetry oracle; both retained pre-correction trajectories fail five collider-bound checks.
adjudication.decision: Replace only the canonical CUDA rigid-direct golden with the corrected clean-revision CUDA trajectory. Preserve the historical raw captures and unchanged direct tolerance.

replacement.reference_regression: PASS: one case, zero differences at the canonical five checkpoints

reproduction: Build commit d6310bf9b65d81f8c30b2d45e415c43b82396249 with the Slang CPU conformance configuration and with the native Windows Slang CUDA configuration.
Set PM_DRIVER_FILES and PM_LAYER_FILES to each build's generated driver and validation manifests, then run parallel-mater-conformance --case rigid-direct --every-frame --output <backend-output>.
Run conformance/v1/quality.py with rigid-kinematic-sweep-v1.json against each every-frame result.
Run conformance/v1/compare.py with the CUDA every-frame directory as expected and CPU as actual; retain the unchanged-tolerance failure.
Run each backend without --every-frame, replace only golden/cuda/rigid-direct.json with the reviewed CUDA result, then compare both backends against the replacement.
limitations: CPU does not pass the replacement CUDA trajectory at the unchanged direct tolerance; F5-18 owns the single bounded planar-symmetry component.
Passing the independent sweep oracle establishes this fixture's physical response, not broad rigid, CUDA, CPU, Gallery, performance or driver qualification.
The complete CUDA registry still contains the five retained process crashes and other reference-regression failures documented by F5-11.
